item.title: #3594817: The judge prompt fence can be closed with an upper-case tag
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Minor bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 85 files, +2438/−224 · php +2301/−210 · md +134/−14 · css +2 · yml +1
  • Diff: 2fa03ac
  • Discussion: #3594817 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The judge prompt in AI Eval wraps the question, criteria and the evaluated answer in XML-style tags. Before this fix, only the exact lower-case closing tags were neutralised. An answer containing </AGENT_RESPONSE> or a closing tag with extra spaces could close the answer section early, so any text after it might read to the judge as instructions. Closing fence tags are now escaped in any letter case and with spacing or attributes. The reporter did not test whether a judge model actually follows such text, so this is a hardening measure. Updating is enough; the 1.1.x changelog and judge documentation were updated to describe it.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Low-priority prompt-injection hardening: an answer could close the judge prompt's <agent_response>, <question> or <criteria> fence with </AGENT_RESPONSE> or </agent_response >. Those variants are now escaped.

Technical details

LlmJudgeBase::escapePromptValue() replaced its three-pair str_replace() with a case-insensitive preg_replace(). It matches < followed by /, optional whitespace, then question, criteria or agent_response, and anything up to the closing >. It prefixes a backslash after the <, so </AGENT_RESPONSE> becomes <\/AGENT_RESPONSE>. The inner text is otherwise untouched, so the judge still sees the original content. The method also changed from private to public static. The issue proposed a pattern allowing only whitespace inside the tag, and the merged pattern also covers attributes. The commit also contains the other 1.1.x judge-trust changes (#3594812, #3594813, #3594814, #3594815, #3594816). They are not part of this fix, and I did not read the LlmJudgeBase.php hunks for them beyond the escape function.

item.title: #3594816: Judge validation counts a judge error as a fail verdict
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 85 files, +2438/−224 · php +2301/−210 · md +134/−14 · css +2 · yml +1
  • Diff: 2fa03ac
  • Discussion: #3594816 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Judge validation used to count a labeled answer the judge never scored (a provider error, a rate limit, or a judge with no model) as a judge fail. That inflated the true negative rate on fail-labeled rows and added false negatives on pass-labeled rows. Such answers are now left out of the confusion matrix and the rates, and shown as Not scored on the validation report, history, Judges page and drush ai-eval:judges. Any not-scored labeled answer blocks the Trusted state. Run database updates and validate again any judge that had provider errors, because earlier stored counts cannot be repaired. The same commit also ships related trust changes: a minimum of 10 distinct pass and 10 distinct fail labels (new Not enough labels state), and stricter threshold handling.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Database update: ai_eval_update_10050 adds nullable not_scored, endpoint_only, pass_items and fail_items columns to ai_eval_judge_validation.
  • Config change: Pass thresholds now accept at most two decimals (form step changed from 0.1 to 0.01).
  • API change: JudgeValidationReport gains optional trailing $notScored, $passItems, $failItems, $endpointOnly constructor arguments; JudgeValidationStoreInterface, JudgeGateTrustInterface and CorrectedPassRateInterface gain methods that custom implementations must add.
  • New API: JudgeValidationReport::trustBlocker(), passLabels(), failLabels(), trustState() and a new not_enough_labels trust state.

Technical details

In JudgeValidator::validate(), a labeled row with a NULL graderScore now increments $notScored and is skipped before TP/FP/FN/TN. The correlation and calibration arrays already skipped NULL scores. RepeatedVerdicts::group() now records verdicts only for scored repeats, so an item with no scored repeat has an empty verdict list. The error profile, stability and judge comparison skip those items, and the comparison reports them as not scored (notScoredA/notScoredB on JudgeComparisonResult).

JudgeValidationReport::trustBlocker() returns the first blocker in order: BLOCKER_NOT_SCORED (any notScored > 0), BLOCKER_FEW_LABELS (fewer than MIN_LABELS_PER_CLASS = 10 distinct scored pass or fail items), then BLOCKER_RATES (TPR or TNR under 0.90). isTrusted() is now true only when there is no blocker. The not_scored, pass_items, fail_items and endpoint_only values are stored on ai_eval_judge_validation, NULL meaning not recorded for older rows. drush ai-eval:validate-judge prints a specific warning for each blocker and exits 3 when the fixture has too few labels.

The commit also bundles other changes tracked in separate issues, listed in the CHANGELOG: the corrected pass rate requires validation at the run's threshold (#3594814), the label minimum (#3594813), stale trust after a prompt edit (#3594812), fence-tag escaping (#3594817) and % handling in prompt templates (#3594815). Scores are now compared with ScoreScale::passes() so validation and run scoring use the same two-decimal rounding.

Upgrade

Run database updates (ai_eval_update_10050). Existing validation rows get NULL for the new columns. Validate again any judge that had provider errors.

Custom code that constructs JudgeValidationReport can pass the new optional trailing arguments $notScored, $passItems, $failItems and $endpointOnly. Custom implementations or mocks of JudgeValidationStoreInterface (four new methods), JudgeGateTrustInterface and CorrectedPassRateInterface (new thresholdMismatch()) must add them. A CI gate on the exit code of drush ai-eval:validate-judge can start failing with code 3 if the fixture has fewer than 10 distinct scored pass or fail items.

item.title: #3594815: A "%" in a judge prompt template stops the run
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 85 files, +2438/−224 · php +2301/−210 · md +134/−14 · css +2 · yml +1
  • Diff: 2fa03ac
  • Discussion: #3594815 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

A "%" in a judge's prompt template (for example "score 100% of the facts") no longer stops the whole run. The Edit prompt tab now refuses a template that does not have exactly four %s placeholders, and tells you to write %% for a literal percent sign. A template saved earlier that no longer fits now makes each answer it scores an error with a clear reason, not a failed run. A template that leaves out the answer placeholder also scores nothing and reports an error, where before the judge was asked without the answer. The same commit also bundles several related judge trust changes (#3594812, #3594813, #3594814, #3594816, #3594817), which are listed in the changelog.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Database update: The commit also ships ai_eval_update_10050, adding nullable not_scored, endpoint_only, pass_items and fail_items columns to ai_eval_judge_validation (from the bundled trust changes, not this issue's fix).

Technical details

LlmJudgeBase::grade() used to call sprintf($template, ...) outside its try, so an ArgumentCountError from a stray % escaped and ended the browser or Drush run. The call now sits inside the try, preceded by a new public static LlmJudgeBase::templateCheck(). It formats the template with four marker strings and returns throws (formatting failed) and missing (slot numbers whose marker is absent from the output). If it throws, or slot 4 (the answer) is missing, grade() returns an errored result with a judge error: message and does not call the model. Missing slots 1 to 3 are not blocked at run time.

JudgePromptEditForm::validateForm() uses the same templateCheck(). It rejects a template that throws, and one that leaves out any of the four placeholders, naming the omitted slots. The field description now mentions %%, and the save message tells the user to validate the judge again. LlmJudgeBase also gains hasResolvedPrompt(), which reports whether the latest attempt resolved a prompt and version, including errored attempts. escapePromptValue() became public static and now escapes closing question, criteria and agent_response fence tags in any letter case, with spaces or attributes.

The commit is large (85 files) and bundles other work. The partial diff I could read shows judge trust gating: a minimum of 10 distinct pass and 10 fail labels, a new not_enough_labels state, not-scored answers blocking trust, and a threshold-matched corrected pass rate. The prompt-version staleness behaviour, ScoreScale::passes() rounding and the two-decimal threshold validation in the settings, target and guided-test forms also appear in the diff. I did not read the omitted files, including JudgeTrustReason, ValidationCompare and the store implementation.

Upgrade

Review any saved judge prompt overrides. A literal percent sign must be written as %%, and the template needs exactly four %s placeholders (dimension, question, expectations, answer). Re-saving an override on the judge's Edit prompt tab runs the new check. Also run drush updatedb, because the commit adds ai_eval_update_10050.

item.title: #3594814: Corrected pass rate ignores the judge's validation threshold
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 85 files, +2438/−224 · php +2301/−210 · md +134/−14 · css +2 · yml +1
  • Diff: 2fa03ac
  • Discussion: #3594814 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The corrected pass rate on a result page now appears only when the judge was validated at the same question pass threshold the run used. Before, a judge validated at 3.0 could correct a run scored at 3.5 with no warning, which gave a number nobody had measured. When the thresholds differ, or the result did not record its threshold, the Corrected Pass Rate row reads "Not available" with both thresholds, and the EEE export leaves the corrected value out. The fix is to validate the judge again at the threshold the run used. Existing results can change to Not available after the update. A validation where the judge only ever scored 0 or 5 is exempt, since every threshold in between gives the same verdict. Older validations need a rerun to record that evidence. The same commit also ships several related judge-trust fixes (#3594812, #3594813, #3594815, #3594816, #3594817).

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Database update: ai_eval_update_10050 adds nullable endpoint_only, not_scored, pass_items and fail_items columns to ai_eval_judge_validation.
  • Config change: Question pass thresholds (site settings, target form, guided test form) now accept at most two decimals; the number step changed from 0.1 to 0.01.
  • API change: CorrectedPassRateInterface::forResult() and bootstrapForResult() take an optional $runThreshold; omitting it returns NULL (no correction). New thresholdMismatch() method on CorrectedPassRateInterface and JudgeGateTrustInterface, so custom implementations and mocks must add it.
  • New API: ScoreScale::passes(), ScoreScale::sameThreshold() and ScoreScale::thresholdMismatch() give one shared pass decision and threshold comparison.

Technical details

CorrectedPassRate::forResult() and bootstrapForResult() now require a recorded $runThreshold and a compatible validation threshold. The compatibility check is ScoreScale::thresholdMismatch(). Thresholds match when they agree at two decimals, and a positive threshold that rounds to zero never matches zero. Otherwise, a validation flagged endpoint_only fits any run threshold above 0 and up to 5. The evidence is measured from the scores (new endpoint_only column), not inferred from a judge's name or declared range. Legacy rows have NULL there, so they get no exemption.

A new thresholdMismatch() method on CorrectedPassRate returns the two thresholds for an otherwise eligible judge. EvalResultsController reads the run threshold from question_pass_threshold in the dataset snapshot. When no correction is produced, it renders the "Not available" message, with a separate wording when the run recorded no threshold.

To make "same threshold" mean the same thing in both places, validation and run scoring now share ScoreScale::passes(), which compares the score rounded to two decimals. LabeledExample::graderPassesAt() and the result page's low-score check both use it. Before, a score of 3.496 at threshold 3.5 failed validation but passed a run. The threshold inputs on the settings, target and guided test forms now use step 0.01 and reject more than two decimals. The validation controller applies the same rule. Docs in scoring.md, judges.md and the EEE export docs, plus the CHANGELOG, were updated.

Upgrade

Run database updates: ai_eval_update_10050 adds the nullable endpoint_only column (and the other new validation columns). Existing validation rows keep NULL there, so they get no endpoint-only exemption. Validate such judges again at the threshold your tests use to get a corrected pass rate.

Custom code that implements or mocks CorrectedPassRateInterface or JudgeGateTrustInterface must add thresholdMismatch(). Callers must pass the run's threshold, or no correction is returned:

$corrected = $correctedPassRate->forResult($graderIds, $p, $ciLow, $ciHigh, $runThreshold);
$bootstrap = $correctedPassRate->bootstrapForResult($graderIds, $scoresJson, $seed, $runThreshold);

item.title: #3594813: A judge can be trusted on two labeled examples
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 85 files, +2438/−224 · php +2301/−210 · md +134/−14 · css +2 · yml +1
  • Diff: 2fa03ac
  • Discussion: #3594813 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

A judge is now Trusted only if it was scored on at least 10 distinct pass labels and 10 distinct fail labels, in addition to TPR and TNR of at least 0.90. Before, one pass and one fail label could both agree and earn the Trusted badge. A validation below the floor now shows a new Not enough labels state (with the counts) on the Judges page, the target list, result pages and in Drush. A repeated score of the same answer counts once. Existing validations below the floor read Not enough labels after the update. The drush ai-eval:validate-judge command exits with code 3 when the fixture is under the floor, so a CI gate built on it can start failing until you add labels. The floor is fixed at 10 per class. The gold_target_n setting is documented as a labeling target, not the minimum. Docs note that a 70/30 split of a small set rarely reaches the minimum.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Database update: ai_eval_update_10050 adds nullable not_scored, endpoint_only, pass_items and fail_items columns to ai_eval_judge_validation.
  • API change: JudgeValidationReport gains optional trailing constructor arguments ($notScored, $passItems, $failItems, $endpointOnly). JudgeValidationStoreInterface, JudgeGateTrustInterface and CorrectedPassRateInterface gain methods that custom implementations and mocks must add.
  • New API: New trust state not_enough_labels (JudgeValidationStoreInterface::STATE_NOT_ENOUGH_LABELS) and JudgeValidationReport::MIN_LABELS_PER_CLASS (10), trustBlocker(), passLabels(), failLabels().

Technical details

The rule lives in JudgeValidationReport::trustBlocker(), which returns the first blocker in precedence order: not-scored answers, fewer than MIN_LABELS_PER_CLASS labels in either class, then the existing rate check against TRUST_THRESHOLD. isTrusted() is now trustBlocker() === NULL, and the new trustState() maps a few-labels blocker to not_enough_labels. The chosen rule is a fixed floor of 10 per class, not the gold_target_n floor or the bootstrap confidence interval option the issue proposed.

Label counts come from new pass_items and fail_items columns (distinct scored items, so repeats count once). Older rows have NULL there, and passLabels() and failLabels() fall back to tp + fn and fp + tn, which include repeats. The update hook adds the columns as nullable and does not recompute. The new state is wired through JudgeTrustBadge, JudgeTrustMark, EvalTargetListBuilder (counted among the not-trusted states and ranked in TRUST_SEVERITY), the Judges table legend and CSS class ai-eval-trust--not_enough_labels. The Drush command prints a specific warning with the pass and fail counts.

The same commit also ships sibling changes from the issues listed in the CHANGELOG: not-scored answers blocking trust (#3594816), a corrected pass rate that requires validation at the run's threshold (#3594814), stale trust after a prompt edit (#3594812), fence-tag escaping (#3594817) and prompt template % handling (#3594815). Pass thresholds now accept at most two decimals. The diff was partly truncated, so those parts are described from the CHANGELOG and the visible hunks.

Upgrade

Run database updates so ai_eval_update_10050 adds the new columns. Existing validations below 10 pass or 10 fail labels then read Not enough labels. Older rows lack distinct-label counts and use judgment counts, which include repeats. Validate again on more labels to record exact counts. A CI gate on drush ai-eval:validate-judge can start exiting with code 3 until the fixture has at least 10 distinct scored pass items and 10 fail items.

Custom implementations of JudgeValidationStoreInterface, JudgeGateTrustInterface and CorrectedPassRateInterface, and mocks of them, must add the new methods (thresholdMismatch() among them). JudgeValidationReport has new optional trailing constructor arguments, so existing calls keep working.

  • Committed: October 31, 2026 (6 days later)

item.title: #3594812: A judge stays trusted after its prompt is edited
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 85 files, +2438/−224 · php +2301/−210 · md +134/−14 · css +2 · yml +1
  • Diff: 2fa03ac
  • Discussion: #3594812 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

A judge validated on one prompt used to keep showing Trusted after you edited its template or guidance, and a gate with refuse_unvalidated_judges still accepted it. Now the judge shows Validation out of date, with a reason naming the validated and current prompt versions. This applies on the Judges page, result pages and the test list. A judge validated on the default prompt also goes out of date once any override is saved. Judges validated from a CLI fixture measure no prompt, so they go out of date as soon as the judge has an override. Validate again in the browser to clear it. The same release commit also adds other judge-trust rules (minimum labels, unscored answers, threshold matching for the corrected pass rate).

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Database update: ai_eval_update_10050 adds nullable not_scored, pass_items, fail_items and endpoint_only columns to ai_eval_judge_validation. The commit bundles several related judge-trust changes.
  • Config change: Pass thresholds in the settings, target and guided test forms now accept at most two decimals (step 0.01).
  • New API: JudgeValidationStoreInterface gains validatedVersionMatches() and activePromptVersion() (plus other methods from the same commit); custom implementations and mocks must add them.

Technical details

JudgeValidationStore::trustStateForRow() now returns STATE_STALE for an otherwise trusted row when validatedVersionMatches() is FALSE, in the same place as the existing model-mismatch check. validatedVersionMatches() compares the row's config_version (NULL means the default template) with activePromptVersion(), which reads JudgeConfigStore::activeOverride(). The store service now receives @ai_eval.judge_config_store. If no config store is injected, the match is unknown (NULL) and the state is unchanged. Saving only the model or domain tags does not bump the prompt version, so only the existing model rule applies there.

The reason text comes from the new JudgeTrustReason::forRow(). The Judges page shows the version column as v1 (now v2). drush ai-eval:validate-judge prints a note when the judge has an override, because a fixture validation records no config_version. Trust is evaluated when a page opens, so results stored earlier also lose their Trusted mark and corrected rate after a prompt edit. The docs (judges.md) and CHANGELOG were updated.

The commit is a combined release commit: it also introduces the not_enough_labels state (fewer than 10 distinct pass or fail labels), not_scored handling, threshold-matched corrected pass rates, and fence-tag and % template fixes, tracked in separate issues (#3594813, #3594814, #3594815, #3594816, #3594817).

Upgrade

Run database updates (ai_eval_update_10050). After editing a judge's template or guidance, validate the judge again in the browser. CLI fixture validations record no prompt version, so they also read Validation out of date once an override exists. Custom implementations or mocks of JudgeValidationStoreInterface must add validatedVersionMatches(object $row): ?bool and activePromptVersion(string $graderId): ?int.

item.title: #3594834: Trace import shows a structured ai_observability span as one user message holding raw JSON
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 34 files, +2626/−156 · php +2075/−154 · json +478 · md +58/−2 · css +14 · txt +1
  • Diff: d49d3a8
  • Discussion: #3594834 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Trace import in ai_eval now handles the structured JSON that ai_observability writes by default. Before, a structured span showed up in trace review as one user message full of raw JSON, and tool calls were lost. Messages now appear as separate messages, tool calls show on the review card, and the reply is the reply text. Spans that ai_observability cut or summarized are flagged and cannot be promoted, and neither can traces with tool calls or tool results in their input, because replay cannot send those yet. The importer also no longer drops every document after a stray closing brace in a trace file. It reports how many parts were skipped, and warns when the rest of a file was not read because of an unclosed brace. The warnings appear on the import page and in drush ai-eval:import-traces. Plain role-line input is read more reliably too: text before the first role line is kept, Windows line endings work, and developer is shown as system.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New Drupal\ai_eval\Service\TracePayloadParser with parseInput(), parseOutput(), parsePlain() and hasCutSignature(), and TraceImporter::splitDocumentsWithReport().

Technical details

The new TracePayloadParser replaces OtelTraceSource::parseMessages(). parseInput() treats input starting with {"messages":[ as structured. It keeps each message's role and text, each assistant message's tool calls (id, name, arguments as a string) and each tool message's tool_id. Anything else goes through parsePlain(). parseOutput() uses normalized.text and normalized.tools when the output is a chat normalized object. Other outputs, such as embeddings, are returned unchanged.

Cut detection does not depend on the 1024 default. hasCutSignature() looks for the [...] marker at the midpoint position where ai_observability's truncation puts it, for strings of at least 32 characters. When a payload is cut, only complete leading message objects from the retained head are recovered. Flags (input_cap, output_cap, omitted, shortened) land in payload_flags on the normalized trace, set truncated, and drive the review card notices. OtlpSpanMapper also uses these checks when setting the stored truncated column. Normalized traces gain raw_input, input_format, response_tools, response_incomplete and payload_flags.

PromotionService has a new STATUS_TOOL_TURNS (tool_turns) refusal. It applies to structured input containing tool role messages, tool calls or call ids. Promoted questions now store metadata.raw_input (up to 8000 characters) and, for tool-only replies, metadata.ai_response_tools as a JSON string. Both are strings so questions stay editable. The streamed_uncaptured check no longer fires when the reply has tool calls or was cut.

On the document side, TraceImporter::splitDocumentsWithReport() scans depth-zero objects with a string-aware matcher. Stray text, stray } and closed non-OTLP objects are skipped and logged with a byte offset. An unclosed object or string stops the read, since later objects could be nested payload data. ImportResult gains skippedDocuments and unreadTails. splitDocuments() still exists and delegates to the new method.

Upgrade

Spans already imported keep their stored truncated value, so re-import them to get the new cut and summarized flags. Parsing of messages and replies happens when a trace is read. Observed tool calls do not fill Expected tools during promotion.

item.title: #3594820: Trace messages split, or lose text, when a line is only a role name
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 34 files, +2626/−156 · php +2075/−154 · json +478 · md +58/−2 · css +14 · txt +1
  • Diff: d49d3a8
  • Discussion: #3594820 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Trace review and promotion in ai_eval 1.1.x now read traces more faithfully. Text before the first role line is kept as a user message instead of being lost, Windows line endings and developer messages work, and a role word inside a list no longer produces empty messages. Promoted questions keep the raw input text in their metadata. The structured JSON that ai_observability writes by default is now read as messages, tool calls and reply text. Spans that ai_observability cut or summarized are marked and cannot be promoted. Traces with tool calls in their input also cannot be promoted yet, because replay cannot send those turns. Trace import no longer drops every document after a stray closing brace. The import page and drush ai-eval:import-traces now report how many parts were skipped and when the rest of a file was not read. The commit bundles the fixes for #3594820, #3594819 and #3594834.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: Promoted questions gain metadata.raw_input and, for tool-only replies, metadata.ai_response_tools.
  • New API: New Drupal\ai_eval\Service\TracePayloadParser with parsePlain(), parseInput(), parseOutput() and hasCutSignature(); new TraceImporter::splitDocumentsWithReport().

Technical details

The old OtelTraceSource::parseMessages() is replaced by TracePayloadParser, which has no container dependency. parsePlain() normalizes line endings and maps developer to system. It treats a role line directly after another role marker as content, because the producer writes an empty turn as a blank line. Leading text becomes a user message. The format has no escaping, so a bare user or tool line after a text line can still split a message. This is documented, and the raw input is stored to compensate. parseInput() and parseOutput() detect structured payloads ({"messages":[ and {"normalized":{"role":). They recover only complete leading messages from a capped payload and never fabricate missing text. They report flags (input_cap, output_cap, omitted, shortened), including the ai_observability middle [...] marker at any length limit of at least 32 characters. Non-chat output is passed through unchanged.

OtlpSpanMapper now sets truncated for any of these signals. PromotionService gains STATUS_TOOL_TURNS. It refuses structured input with tool roles, tool calls or call ids, and no longer calls a tool-only reply streamed_uncaptured. promotionIntegrityFlag() is unchanged for plain input. The question metadata gets raw_input (capped at 8000 characters) and, for tool-only replies, ai_response_tools as a JSON string. TraceReviewFragment renders tool calls, results matched to call names, and warning notices.

On the import side, TraceImporter::splitDocumentsWithReport() replaces the brace-depth scanner. It skips stray text, stray closing braces and closed non-documents, and counts each one. It never restarts inside a candidate, so nested payload objects are not imported as documents. An unclosed object or an unterminated string (a raw line break ends a string) stops the read and sets an unread-tail count. ImportResult carries skippedDocuments and unreadTails. TraceImportBatch and EvalImportTracesCommand show them as warnings. Drush still exits 0 when at least one document was read.

Upgrade

Traces imported before this change keep their stored truncated value. The new payload flags are also computed when a trace is read, so older rows with cut or summarized structured payloads are now shown with notices and refused for promotion. Re-import is only needed for traces whose files had damaged parts that were previously dropped.

item.title: #3594819: One malformed document in a trace file drops every document after it
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 34 files, +2626/−156 · php +2075/−154 · json +478 · md +58/−2 · css +14 · txt +1
  • Diff: d49d3a8
  • Discussion: #3594819 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Importing OTLP trace files in ai_eval 1.1.x no longer silently loses documents. Before, one stray } or one unclosed { made the importer drop every later document in the file, with no warning. Now a stray closing brace, stray text or a closed object that is not a trace document is skipped and counted, and later documents are still imported. An unclosed brace or unterminated string stops the read for that file. The import page and drush ai-eval:import-traces warn about both cases. The same commit also changed trace review: it reads the structured JSON that ai_observability writes by default, shows tool calls, and marks cut spans as not promotable. It also fixes role-line parsing (#3594834, #3594820). If you imported trace files before, re-import any that had damaged parts.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New public static TraceImporter::splitDocumentsWithReport() returning docs, skipped and unread counts; ImportResult gains skippedDocuments and unreadTails; new PromotionService::STATUS_TOOL_TURNS.

Technical details

TraceImporter::splitDocuments() now delegates to the new splitDocumentsWithReport(). It scans for depth-zero objects with a string-aware objectEnd() and never restarts a scan inside a candidate. Decision answers recorded while a new entity is being saved (for example by a Direct field automator running during presave) used to be stored with no entity link and no kept text, and were never deleted with the entity. They counted toward the caller's "Stop after" limit but could not be reviewed properly. They are now linked to the entity, with the kept text, once the entity is saved, and are deleted with it. Summary

The Tool module's AI connector (tool_ai_connector) used to drop arguments it didn't recognize. A model that misspelled an input name only heard that the input it meant was missing, so it retried with the same wrong key. The connector now reports the unrecognized name, for example numbr: This input is not defined for the tool., and the tool doesn't run. Summary

The usage line printed by drush tool:info now uses the first example declared on an input definition instead of a made-up value. Before this, a tool declaring examples: ['Oma'] still showed "word":"example_word" in the usage line, even though the JSON Schema printed just above listed Oma. Inputs with no declared examples keep the generated placeholder values.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

In ToolInfoCommand, getExampleValue() now takes the InputDefinitionInterface instead of a data type string. It returns reset($definition->getExamples()) when examples exist. Otherwise, for a ListInputDefinition it returns a one-item list built recursively from getItemDefinition(), so nested lists produce [[1]]. For anything else it uses the existing match on data type. A declared example of 0 is honored, because the check is !== [] rather than a truthiness test. The change applies to both the table and markdown output formats. New tests in ToolInfoCommandTest cover declared examples on example_values_tool (field_tags, 0, ["alpha"]) and list fallbacks on recursive_scalar_transform_tool.

item.title: #3583053: MapAdapter discards default values of nested properties
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +418/−5 · php +418/−5
  • Diff: 4eaacb0
  • Discussion: #3583053 · 1 contributor · 18 comments

Summary

Map inputs in the Tool module's configuration forms now show their nested properties' declared default values. Before, the property fields of a map input rendered empty. Each field now shows the stored value if there is one, otherwise the property's declared default. This applies at every level of a nested map. Entity properties inside a map also show the right entity when the value is an entity ID.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

MapAdapter::formElement() now reads the map's current value and calls setValue() on each property's typed data before building its element. It uses the stored value when the key exists, including a stored FALSE. Otherwise it uses the property's declared default. A property stored as NULL stays empty, so a cleared value does not bring the default back. A nested map stored as NULL is built like an empty map, so its own properties show their defaults. A value the property cannot hold throws \InvalidArgumentException, which is caught and the value dropped.

Core MapDataDefinition properties have no default of their own, so EffectiveDataDefinition::copyPropertyDefinitions() now copies the default of each InputDefinitionInterface property into a new EffectiveDataDefinition::DEFAULT_VALUE_SETTING (tool_default_value) setting on the rebuilt definition. Output definitions do not get it. EffectiveDataDefinition is @internal.

EntityAdapter gets a private getEntity() helper. A map property's stored value or default is often an entity ID rather than an entity object, so the helper loads the content entity by ID. It returns NULL for config entity types, IDs that do not load, other value shapes, and definitions with no fixed entity type. The helper result feeds both the target type and #default_value of the autocomplete. New kernel tests cover MapAdapter defaults and EntityAdapter ID handling.

item.title: #3583059: Config entities do not cross a handle boundary
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 1.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 10 files, +441/−30 · php +427/−29 · md +14/−1
  • Diff: 1c8757e
  • Discussion: #3583059 · 1 contributor · 9 comments

Summary

Tools can now take and return config entities, such as user roles, through invokers that ask for entity handles, for example an MCP server or the AI connector. Before, the input schema had no type, so a model didn't know what to send. Sending a machine name failed validation. Config entity outputs came out as empty objects. Now these entities cross the boundary as their machine name (for example editor) and the schema says string. An unknown machine name fails the input with a clear error. Content entities still use handles, and invokers without EntitiesAsHandles see no change.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: EntityHandleTransformer gains public isConfigEntityDefinition(), resolveConfigInput() and transformConfigOutput(). New MachineNameNotFoundException implements HandleExceptionInterface.

Technical details

When the invoker has InvokerCapability::EntitiesAsHandles, EntityHandleTransformer::isConfigEntityDefinition() detects an entity:TYPE definition whose entity class implements ConfigEntityInterface. transformInputDefinition() and transformOutputDefinition() turn it into a string definition, with "(pass the machine name of the TYPE)" appended to the description for inputs. The bare entity data type is not covered, because the entity type is needed to load by ID.

On input, EntityHandleTransformSubscriber checks for a config entity definition before the content entity case. It calls resolveConfigInput(), which loads the entity through the type's storage. Non-string values pass through untouched. On output, transformConfigOutput() replaces a config entity with its ID and a hint. The batch path handles lists, either isMultiple() outputs or ListOutputDefinition items. It replaces each config entity with its ID and adds one hint per list, such as "Output roles contains 2 user_role machine name(s)".

An unknown machine name throws the new Drupal\tool\Handle\MachineNameNotFoundException. It is final, extends \RuntimeException and implements HandleExceptionInterface. It is separate from HandleNotFoundException, so a wrong value does not get the advice about handle expiry and ownership. The input violation names the input property. The commit adds a config_entity_tool test tool in tool_test and updates the handle docs.

Upgrade

Code that catches HandleExceptionInterface already covers the new MachineNameNotFoundException. Code that catches HandleNotFoundException specifically will not see unknown machine names, and needs to catch the new class or the interface.
